messages:
deploy-bot: Starting canary rollout: model-inference:v4.0 (tokenizer bundle tk3.0) -> canary traffic 5% in hosted/us-east-1

incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: tokenization-error-rate exceeded for model-inference:v4.0 (canary). Routed to #incidents and @sre-oncall.

maya: seeing a sharp jump in tokenization_errors at 14:03 UTC. Lots of responses with repeated [UNK] and broken detokenization.

sam: customer-reports inbound: app-tier-9 reporting corrupted outputs for chat completions. They pasted examples — whole sentences turning into token ids.

jun: heads-up: this rollout included tokenizer package tk3.0 (packaging change) plus a weight layout tweak. Build meta: v4.0+tk3.0+layoutB.

oliver: can we get an example log? trying to triage whether this is tokenizer mismatch or model weight ordering.

maya: logs attached below:

```
E Tokenizer::DecodeError at token_decode.cc:76 - invalid token sequence (id=65535)
  at Tokenizer::decode(token_decode.cc:76)
  at Serve::handle_request(serve.cc:512)
```

sam: that looks like a tokenizer decode failure. but some replies also show collapsed logits which smells like model artifact mismatch.

sre-oncall: I'm on it. oliver, please confirm who can flip the rollout flag. jun, can you stage a rollback?

oliver: I can flip the model_rollout_v4.0 flag in the console or via CLI. standing by to toggle.

jun: preparing rollback artifact to v3.9 with tokenizer pinned to tk2.7. Also crafting a quick patch to revert the packaging change.

sre-oncall: do the flag flip first to stop more users hitting the canary. oliver, toggle now.

oliver: /ff set model_rollout_v4.0 false -> executed at 14:07 UTC
deploy-bot: Feature flag changed: model_rollout_v4.0 OFF by oliver. Canary traffic routing reverted to model-inference:v3.9.

sre-oncall: monitoring metrics. maya, watch tokenization_errors and sampling for the previously failing prompt set.

maya: errors drop to baseline within ~40s after the flag flip. sample outputs for previously failing prompts look normal again.

sam: sent note to app-tier-9 support: "We've rolled back a canary change that affected tokenization; your requests should be returning to normal. We'll follow up with a detailed incident summary." They replied :thumbsup:.

jun: pushed rollback command to control plane: `revert-deploy --service model-inference --to v3.9 --pin-tokenizer=tk2.7 --reason "canary tokenizer regression"`

deploy-bot: Rollback accepted: model-inference:v3.9 (tk2.7) pinned and promoted for canary.

sre-oncall: observability shows latency and success-rate back to normal within 3m. no downstream writes impacted.

oliver: temporary mitigation note: disabling automatic tokenizer bundle upgrades in packaging pipeline until we add tokenizer compatibility checks.

maya: collecting artifacts for RCA: failing inputs, detokenizer traces, packaging diff (commit 9f2d1b4 -> tk3.0), sampling logs.

sam: customer impact assessment: approx 1.2% of requests during the canary window (14:03-14:07 UTC) experienced decode failures or garbled outputs; ~8 affected enterprise requests. No sensitive data exposed. All affected traffic rerouted within 1 minute of flag flip.

sre-oncall: marking SEV2. postmortem required. oliver will own remediation items. handoff to oliver for follow-ups.

oliver: follow-ups I'm owning: (1) revert tokenizer packaging change, (2) add tokenizer smoke tests to CI and pre-canary gating, (3) add explicit tokenizer pinning step to release runbook. ETA for PRs and tests: 72h.

jun: opened packaging PR to pin tokenizers and add a preflight: https://git.internal/r/redwood/packaging/pull/489 (draft).

maya: I'll start the incident writeup with timeline, customer comms draft, and mitigation steps. pinging for review.

incident-bot: Pager resolved. Incident mitigated by feature-flag rollback and pinned rollback release. Duration: 4m 12s. Owners: oliver, jun, maya. :white_check_mark:

sre-oncall: nice work everyone. we'll hold off public status update until the postmortem is complete. thanks for the quick response.
